- When sentiment is consistently negative (last 3–5 days), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–4% above recent high.
- If sentiment turns positive mid-horizon, model fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per positive sentiment shift.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Lagged sentiment: if sentiment was positive 5–7 days ago, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to compensate.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate early in the horizon (first 7–10 days); apply linear decay correction (reduce by 0.1–0.3% per day).
